sentences.text: Revenue went from $114 billion in FY2016 [F1] to $184 billion in FY2025 [F10]; the ten-year CAGR of 5.4% [F177] mixes bases because FY2025 is recast [R3].
On a consistent recast basis, revenue fell at a three-year CAGR of -7.9% from FY2022 to FY2025 [D626].
FY2022 revenue rose 51.5% [D232] and net income reached $35.5 billion [X17], which the filing ties to higher upstream realizations and downstream margins [P55][P56].
FY2023 revenue fell 16.5% [D274] on lower upstream realizations and downstream margins, per the filing [P43][P44].
Chevron U.S.A. Inc. made up 75.1% of FY2025 revenue [D402] and fell 5.3% [D403], subtracting 3.9pp from total growth [D404].
Revenue fell 4.6% to $184 billion [D358][F10] mainly on lower crude oil and refined product prices [P17].
The largest positive contributor was U.S. upstream, up 34.0% [D553] and adding 2.5pp [D554], as Hess and Permian production grew [P24].
Non-US downstream fell 13.1% [D518] and subtracted 4.9pp [D519], the largest negative; the filings in the pack do not explain that segment's fall.
Operating costs fell 3.4% [D373] against revenue's 4.6% [D358], so diluted EPS fell 31.8% [D361] against net income's 30.5% [D359] as shares rose 2.1% [D374].
Cost of revenue was 57.2% of revenue in FY2025 [D338], down from the FY2023 high of 59.3% [D254].
Cost of revenue fell 9.2% [D370], faster than revenue's 4.6% [D358], as purchased crude and products decreased on lower prices and volumes [P14].
Net margin of 6.7% [F30] sits below its window median of 7.9% [D613] and the energy peer median of 10.2% [D632].
D&A rose to $20.1 billion [X70] from $17.3 billion [X69], which the filing ties to higher production and rates [P12].
The effective tax rate rose to 36.8% [D345] from 27.6% [D261], a move that mix effects across jurisdictions can drive [P33].
FY2025 free cash flow was 1.35x net income [D347], above its window median of 1.10x [D622] but below the energy peer median of 1.42x [D640].
Capex was 0.86x D&A [D348] even after 5.5% growth [D364], so near-term free cash flow leans on depreciation running ahead of reinvestment.
Operating cash flow fell 28.2% in FY2023 [D278] on lower upstream realizations and refining margins [P42].
The company guides 2026 organic capex to $18 to $19 billion [P4], above FY2025 capex of $17.3 billion [F70].
Net cash turned positive at $3.96 billion [D351] from net debt of $156 million [D309] in FY2024.
Net cash at 2.1% of revenue [D352] ranks at the 83rd percentile of six energy peers [D637], against a peer median of -7.7% [D638].
Buybacks and dividends of $24.8 billion [D353] were 149.7% of free cash flow [D354], the third straight year above 100% [R4].
Interest expense rose to $1.22 billion [X80] from $594 million [X79], and the filing names higher interest expense as the main driver of higher net charges [P18].
Revenue has fallen three straight years [R1][F8][F9][F10], a three-year CAGR of -7.9% [D626], so the decline is persistent rather than a single-year dip.
Distributions exceeded free cash flow for three years [R4][D270][D312][D354], and cash and investments fell to $7.29 billion [D349] from $8.26 billion [D307].
Revenue for FY2018, FY2019 and FY2021 to FY2025 is a later recast [R3]; FY2025 was $189 billion as first reported [X10] against $184 billion in the table [F10].
Free cash flow of $16.6 billion [F80] must reach $24.8 billion [D353] to cover buybacks and dividends; a rise toward that level in the FY2026 10-K would close the gap.
Net margin back above its window median of 7.9% [D613], from 6.7% [F30], would signal recovery; a fall below 6.7% [F30] would extend the squeeze in the FY2026 10-K.
Capex against the 2026 guidance of $18 to $19 billion [P4], versus $17.3 billion in FY2025 [F70], shows whether free cash flow absorbs the spend in the FY2026 10-K.
